text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on February 6 in history.
1515 - Aldus Manutius, Italian editor and printer, died; he produced the first paperbacks and invented italics.
1564 - Christopher Marlowe, English poet and dramatist, author of "Dr Faustus", born.
1665 - Anne, queen of Great Britain from 1702-14, born; the last of the Stuart monarchs, she was on the throne for the union of England and Scotland in 1707.
1685 - Charles II, king of Great Britain and Ireland, died; James II acceded to the throne.
1783 - Lancelot "Capability" Brown, noted English landscape gardener, died.
1788 - Massachusetts became the 6th of the United States.
1793 - Carlo Goldoni, Italian comic playwright, died; considered the founder of Italian realistic comedy.
1802 - Charles Wheatstone, English physicist and pioneer of telegraphy, born.
1804 - Joseph Priestley, English cleric and chemist, one of the discoverers of oxygen, died.
1838 - Sir Henry Irving, English actor born; he became the first actor to be knighted.
1838 - During the Boers Great Trek, Boer leader Piet Retief was murdered by the Zulu king Dingane's warriors.
1840 - The Treaty of Waitangi was signed under which New Zealand's Maori population accepted Queen Victoria's sovereignty in their lands.
1895 - George Herman "Babe" Ruth, legendary American baseball player, born.
1897 - Alberto Cavalcanti, Brazilian director, producer and screenwriter noted for his documentaries, born.
1905 - Wladyslaw Gomulka, Polish Communist leader from 1956-70, born.
1911 - Ronald Reagan, U.S. actor-turned-politician, born. Governor of California from 1966, he became the 40th president of the United States in 1980 and won a second term from 1984-88.
1912 - Eva Braun, wife of Adolf Hitler, born; they married the day before they committed suicide in their Berlin bunker in April 1945.
1919 - Zsa Zsa Gabor, Hungarian actress renowned more for her marriages than her movies, born.
1922 - The Washington Conference between U.S., France, Japan, Italy and Britain ended with agreement on restricting use of poison gas and submarine warfare.
1931 - Isabel Peron, Argentine dancer who became a political leader and followed her husband Juan as President from 1974-76, born.
1932 - Francois Truffaut, French film director, born; he directed "Jules et Jim" and won an Oscar for "Day for Night".
1952 - King George VI of Great Britain and Northern Ireland died and was succeeded by his daughter, Elizabeth II.

1958 - Seven members of Britain's Manchester United football team were among 21 killed in a plane crash in Munich. Nicknamed the "Busby Babes" after their manager Matt Busby, they were returning from a European Cup match.
1976 - In the U.S., Lockheed Aircraft Corporation admitted it had bribed officials in the Netherlands, Japan, Sweden and Italy.
1994 - Defence Minister Elisabeth Rehn of the Swedish People's Party conceded defeat to Martti Ahtisaari of the opposition Social Democrats in Finland's presidential election.
1994 - Togo held its first multi-party election for parliament.
